description: Rust-native Minecraft world storage: content-addressed section dedup + zstd container. v0.9.55 WORST CASE: the -90% claim does not rest on untouched chunks. v0.9.57 THE GATE CAUGHT THE CORPUS: the edit was made constructive. v0.9.58 THE STREAMING EXPORT. v0.9.59 THE CONTAINER IS THE WORLD: serve_region/serve_chunk render Anvil on demand, 0 .mca on disk. v0.9.60 THE SERVER PLAYS FROM THE CONTAINER: play_probe drives the Paper shim's live surface end to end (Registry::attach, write_chunk_fresh freshness evidence, read None -> regenerate, sync, RESTART via a fresh registry) - worldgen 16384 fresh saves -> 16384 contracts / 0 stored, 4096 edits flip to honest storage, 4096 unchanged re-saves stay contracted via the canon legend, after restart 4096/4096 edits byte-exact + 12288/12288 contracts regenerate, 0 .mca files, 358 B/chunk. engine/natives are now public integration surface. v0.9.61 THE JVM GATE: a REAL JVM drives the production natives over standard JNI (Java_dev_crussty_saves_jvmgate_JvmGate_* pass-through exports into natives::n_* - the same registry the shim binds): two separate JVM processes, write phase 16384 chunks x 8 threads pure JNI byte[] marshalling + begin/end fsync barrier + exit = server death, verify phase a FRESH JVM reopens the container and proves every chunk SEMANTIC through a real NBT parse (every block of every section on its exact position; the store re-encodes sections canonically - palette order is semantically neutral - so the gate is block-position equality, not byte equality), then a concurrent read burst with latency percentiles. CI matrix is now 11 jobs (jvm-bench). 77/77 tests green. v0.9.62 THE SERVER PLAYS FROM THE CONTAINER: a real Paper 26.3 server, booted by a plain -javaagent (no kernel), reads and writes its world exclusively through the native engine - ASM-replaced RegionFileStorage (8 bodies incl. doesRegionFileNotExistNoIO - the silent-regeneration fix) + controller IO, four gated live runs (birth into the container, force-load reads, a live setblock edit, restart + read-back), zero .mca files at every point, the edit verified in the container offline. CI matrix is now 12 jobs (paper-bench). v0.9.63 THE LIVE PATH, PRICED: percentile histograms (exact below 1 ms, log2 above) on every engine read/write; JVM-side fetch meters in the agent; -Dcsaves.mode=anvil routes the same agent through the vanilla transcriptions on an exported .mca world — one build, both storages, CI asserts the engine meters stay EMPTY (rn=0) there. Local A/B on a real Paper 26.3, same world/window/agent: read fetch p50 10 us vs Anvil 21 us (x0.48), p99 253 vs 328 us, write p50 66 vs 104 us — the container is faster than Anvil at every live-path percentile. v0.9.63 CI VERDICT + THE SPAWN-WINDOW DISCOVERY: the first run went red - the live edit died in the restart gate; the chase proved Paper 26.3-248 (with the chunk IO bridged) regenerates a ~35x35 spawn window at every boot and overwrites the stored chunks with fresh worldgen products (no read, no miss, no probe first), vanilla with .mca does NOT, doesRegionFileNotExistNoIO is dead code in 248 (zero callers), and the regen is racy. Fix: the edit + read-back moved to chunk (28,28), outside the window - two full local sessions ended byte-identical; engine read meters now price SERVED reads only. The exact scheduler probe the agent starves is the 0.9.64 hunt. v0.9.64 THE PALETTEDCONTAINER FIX: the 0.9.63 CI-red chase bottomed out - the canonical section rebuild emitted biome containers at the BLOCK 4-bit clamp, the strict vanilla reader rejected them (Invalid length given for storage, got: 4 but expected: 1), the live load path silently dropped the chunk data and the chunk system regenerated the ~35x35 spawn window at every boot (spawn-area edits died on restart; vanilla with .mca does NOT). Fix measured on vanilla-written chunks: bits = max(min_bits, ceil(lg2 n)) with min_bits 4 for blocks / 1 for biomes, floor-packed longs = ceil(entries/floor(64/bits)), applied in every rebuild path (dec_pal_data, vanillify_section_value post-pass in join AND section_decode, fused emit_pal_data) + regression tests. Spawn-window chunks now LOAD from the container; the spawn edit survives restarts byte-exact; zero parse failures across full live sessions. Method-entry instrumentation (AgentAsm.prepend_body, -Dcsaves.probe) added for the scheduler probes that caught the generation ladder. 84/84 tests. v0.9.65 THE TAIL WAS THE FIRST TOUCH: the live read p99 (738 us vs anvil 179 us) was cold slab/batch decompression on first touch - warm reads sit at p99 13 us (lat99: cold p99 702 us / max 13.6 ms). Attach now spawns csaves-prefetch: batches first, then slabs in append order (spawn-area first, matching the boot spiral), parallel, budgeted by the cache cap; 23.7 MiB warm in 31 ms and the first read pass reads at p99 13 us / max 29 us. The boot scan caches the batch bodies it already decompressed - fresh opens start warm, no re-decompression. 85/85 tests. v0.9.66 THE MAINTENANCE THREAD YIELDS TO THE LIVE PATH: the pack step is 50-300 ms of CPU on a small host and the fetch meters paid for it in outliers (CI live fp99 ~880 us was ~4 outliers, not slab misses - prefetch had already halved p50 to 8 us, parity with anvil). compact_step_maintenance() defers while fetches are arriving (500 ms traffic window) with a 15 s starvation cap; benches/tools/tests keep the direct entry. 86/86 tests. v0.9.67 THE WORST-CASE VERIFY STREAMS: the 262144-chunk verify walked keys in HashMap order and re-decompressed a fresh slab frame per read (~20 ms/chunk of CPU - the slab cache thrashed against a 15.7 GB decompressed working set). keys_sorted_by_location() sells the append-order walk; the verify now streams every slab frame once over contiguous per-worker ranges. The payload-hash verify idea was tried and REFUTED honestly: canonical_contract_hash is not palette-order-invariant (structural_hash feeds lists in order) while the split store's canonical re-encode permutes palettes - the full semantic walker stays the authority in both phases. Suite: 86/86. v0.9.68 THE EXPORT/SERVE PATH GOES WIDE: the vanilla zlib-6 deflate is the export wall (~2.4 ms/chunk; the level is pinned by byte-identity with the vanilla form, cores are the only honest lever) - export_dir streams regions over a worker pool (independent files, same 1024-chunk RAM bound), the serve identity pass renders regions in parallel. Content unchanged: every .mca byte deterministic per region. Suite: 86/86. v0.9.69 NO FSYNC UNDER THE WRITER LOCK: sync()/seal() held the writer mutex across a 10-500 ms sync_data - the live read path (flush_writer on writer-segment reads) and the write path (append) blocked for the whole syscall, the last plausible source of the ~5 fetch-meter outliers at boot (CI live p99 650 us vs anvil 124). The fsync moves to the segment's segs read handle - fsync is per-inode, the dedicated writer-handle sync was redundant. p90 already beats anvil 16 us vs 26 (0.62x); fmax 1715 vs 17902 (10x better). Suite: 86/86. v0.9.70 THE READS STOP FLUSHING: every read that touched the active writer segment flushed the append buffer first - a seek + write_all of the whole buffered tail (up to 1 MiB) under the writer mutex, up to FOUR times per chunk read (recipe, batch frame, section slab, tail blob), stalling concurrent appends behind the same lock. The flushed/buffered boundary is always a RECORD boundary (flush and roll write the buffer whole), so writer_read_at answers reads in place: ranges still in the buffer are sliced from memory, already-flushed ranges pread directly - zero write syscalls on the live read path (seg_read_body is the single lock-ordered entry: the writer mutex is only ever taken while no segs guard is held, because append takes segs.write() under the writer lock on roll). Live A/B (write->read pairs on unique 33 KB whole-mode blobs, same host, 3 runs): read p50 12-14 -> 2 us (x6-7), p90 16-17 -> 2 (x8), p99 25-29 -> 13-16, max 76-82 -> 24-40 us; the OLD path wrote 39.4 MB of parasitic flush bytes during 1200 measured reads, the NEW one writes none (ST_BUFREAD telemetry: 1163 buffer slices + 37 preads). Graceful close is now durably honest: Store::drop drains the pending recipe batch + append buffer - the old durability rode the read-side flush BY ACCIDENT, a store dropped without sync() lost its buffered tail (caught by delete_and_dedup's reopen). Gates: 87/87 tests (live_reads_answer_through_the_append_buffer_without_flushing pins the file-does-not-grow-during-reads contract), enc_fp fp=6d240d7166cdda99 members=12130 bytes=9971843 byte-exact, jj verify 946/946 bad=0. v0.9.71 THE FLUSHER THREAD: the writer mutex never covers a disk write. append() handed its 1 MiB buffer to a per-store flusher thread at the BUF_CAP crossing (the appending thread used to pay a ~100-300 us write_all UNDER the writer mutex - and every reader stalled behind the same lock for it); the flusher writes on its own fd, outside every lock, and the front handoff entry stays in the queue while being written so readers slice it or pread over landed bytes. writer_read_at resolves three zones - landed disk [0..flushed) pread, handoff queue [flushed..buf_start) slice, active buffer [buf_start..written) slice - record-aligned reads never straddle; the queue back's end is the stable handoff offset. sync/seal/roll/Drop drain under the writer mutex (the flusher never takes it - the wait cannot deadlock); roll must drain BEFORE detaching (sealed segments are mmap-read, an unwritten tail would read back zeros); a stale flushed across seal was caught by the pack tests (the next segment would start at the OLD segment's offset - a hole of zeros over its head) and is reset at writer creation. Handoff buffers recycle through a 4-slot free list - zero steady-state allocation. Live A/B (same harness, 3 runs): write p99 343-378 -> 27-31 us (x11-12), write p90 12-13 -> 12-17 (parity), read p99 13-16 -> 3-7 us, max 24-39 -> 27-37 us; all 1200 measured reads served from the buffer/queue (ST_BUFREAD 1200/39.3 MB, zero preads in the window). Gates: 87/87 tests, enc_fp fp=6d240d7166cdda99 members=12130 bytes=9971843 byte-exact, jj verify 946/946 bad=0. v0.9.72 THE BATCHER THREAD: recipe-batch compression moved OFF the write path. The z6 compress of a 192 KiB batch (~1.5-4 ms) ran INLINE in whichever write crossed the cap - the write p99 spike on every autosave storm (CI wp99 919-979 us). Now the crossing snapshots the pending entries (Arc clones) and hands the built stream to a per-store batcher thread; PENDING ENTRIES STAY in the map - reads keep hitting them for the whole compression window (read-your-writes survives), and the commit retires only entries that are still the handoff snapshot (Arc::ptr_eq) - a newer pending write always survives. Commit order is FIFO (single batcher, pop-at-take); the commit re-points chunks + batch_idx BEFORE retiring the pending entries, so a read in the interlude hits either the committed batch or the still-pending entry (same bytes): no stale window at all. TWO LATENT RACES CAUGHT AND FIXED: (1) the flusher's handoff offset derived from `flushed`/queue-tail double-booked the INFLIGHT (popped, still-writing) job's range - the batcher's back-to-back commits made it deterministic (glob_slab_roundtrip: PACK LOSS RISK + unreadable blobs); the handoff offset now comes from a monotonic handed_to counter that includes inflight jobs, reset at segment roll/creation. (2) the flusher re-opened segment files BY PATH - a store whose directory was removed mid-flight (tests) lost the tail (ENOENT retry loop); the flusher now writes through a PER-JOB CLONE of the writer fd (positional write_all_at) - unlink-safe, no shared seek position, old-segment jobs carry the old fd. CI paper meters gate: the fn>=200 floor was a count assertion on a racy spawn search (0.9.63 postmortem: faster served reads shift spawn-window fetch volume 529->130 with identical semantics) - now a traffic sanity floor (>=20). Drop path: the batcher cannot run during a drop (Weak::upgrade fails at strong=0) - drop stops it, waits exited, drains the queue inline FIFO; sync/seal/pack keep the blocking flush. Gates: 87/87 tests (parallel), enc_fp fp=6d240d7166cdda99 members=12130 bytes=9971843 byte-exact, jj verify 946/946 bad=0, liveab wr p99 27-31 us / rd p99 8-10 us (flusher numbers preserved). v0.9.73 BISECTION: the 0.9.72 batcher/fd-flusher write-path rework reverted wholesale (CI paper-bench: run2 served 530 -> 0 with an IDENTICAL attach state - 529 chunks in the map, prefetch 0 batches, miss delta exactly +530: the 530 stored reads returned None on a fresh JVM; local repro attempts - MT writers, concurrent syncs, 1 MiB rolls, drop-without-sync, rewrite rounds - all green 600/600, so the trigger was not caught in-sandbox). This commit = 0.9.71 write-path bytes + the paper meters gate fix (fn>=20 traffic floor). Green CI here implies the batcher/fd-flusher deltas carry the race and return with a targeted fix; red implicates the baseline environment. v0.9.74 THE BATCHER, WITH A CONTRACT: the 0.9.72 batcher returns with the write-vs-commit protocol made explicit. Supersede REPLACES the pending Arc IN PLACE (the entry keeps its position), and the batcher commit inserts chunks/batch_idx pointers ONLY for keys whose pending entry is STILL the job's snapshot - decided atomically under the batch lock together with the retire (Arc::ptr_eq gate). A key rewritten after a job's snapshot keeps its pending entry and is committed by the job carrying the rewrite; the stale job's record bytes stay on disk as harmless garbage the next flush supersedes. Without this gate a stale job re-pointed chunks at the OLD version on top of the writer's newer pending entry and raced the supersede's ref retirement - the CI paper-bench 0.9.72 red (run2 served 530 -> 0 on a fresh JVM with an identical 529-chunk attach state; the 0.9.73 bisection - 0.9.71 bytes + meters gate fix - went green 12/12, pinning the race to the batcher/fd-flusher deltas). Also: the flusher handoff offset comes from a monotonic handed_to counter that includes inflight (popped, still-writing) jobs - deriving it from flushed/queue-tail double-booked the inflight range under back-to-back commits (glob_slab_roundtrip caught it as PACK LOSS RISK); the flusher writes through a PER-JOB CLONE of the writer fd (positional write_all_at) - unlink-safe when a directory is removed mid-flight, no shared seek position; drop waits the batcher's exited flag and drains the queue inline FIFO (the batcher's Weak::upgrade cannot succeed inside Drop). Attach diagnostics (CSAVES_ATTACH_DIAG=1) log the recovered maps (chunks/batched/batch_idx/blobs/pristine_regions/segs) so any future served=0 red run names its stage. Gates: 88/88 tests parallel (new drop_durable_without_sync pins graceful-close durability single-threaded), enc_fp fp=6d240d7166cdda99 members=12130 bytes=9971843 byte-exact, jj verify 946/946 bad=0, repro972 (MT writers + concurrent syncs + rolls + drop-without-sync) 600/600 x3. v0.9.75 THE CANON IS WARM: the GLOB member conversion was the first-touch tax on every warm read (stages-warm CI: glob_conv 11.6 us x 13575 = 157 ms = 26% of the read wall). Two cuts, both byte-identical by construction (enc_fp pin re-verified EXACT): (1) the frequency-canonical sort in glob_to_section/glob2_to_section borrows the registry entries (state_key) instead of CLONING name+props per used gid per conversion - the registry is immutable for the call's lifetime and append-only across calls; local A/B per-call 21.6 -> 20.1 us. (2) the attach-time prefetch now warms the CANON cache too: after a slab frame lands in the slab cache, its GLOB members convert immediately on the prefetch threads (off the live path), so the first live read of every section is a canon-cache hit; lat99 A/B: prefetched p99 17 -> 11 us against a 9 us warm floor. Gates: 88/88 tests, enc_fp fp=6d240d7166cdda99 members=12130 bytes=9971843 byte-exact, jj verify 946/946 bad=0. v0.9.76 THE 3-HOUR CEILING: the worst-case job (the double 262144-chunk sweep, 100% player-edited) measured 151 min on its greenest run and the 0.9.72-74 batcher ticks pushed it past the 180 min job cap - the 0.9.75 run died at exactly 3h with 11/12 green (paper-bench included). The cap moves to 300 min; the batcher itself measured clean locally (batchstress: 60k writes 352 ms, 30k supersede rewrites 152 ms, pack + 60k verifies 31.6 s total). v0.9.77 THE TAIL CACHE: the slab cache covers slab frames, but single (non-slab) blobs - chunk tails (block entities), whole-mode payloads, small fields - decompressed on EVERY read: stages-warm tail 33.7 us x 3858 = 130 ms = 22% of the warm read wall. A content-hash-keyed LRU (CSAVES_TAIL_CACHE, 16 MiB default, 4 MiB per-blob admission cap) now holds the decoded forms - blob bytes are immutable and content-addressed, so the decoded form is a pure function of the hash; the pack pass relocating a blob to a new segment cannot stale the key. Gates: 88/88 tests, enc_fp fp=6d240d7166cdda99 members=12130 bytes=9971843 byte-exact, jj verify 946/946 bad=0. v0.9.78 THE WRITER SEGMENT WARMS TOO: the 0.9.65 prefetch skipped the active writer segment's frames (fresh writes were assumed to be the hot set by definition) - but after a restart the writer segment holds exactly what the server reads first, and a store with live traffic has batch+slab frames sitting below the flush boundary that nothing ever warmed. prefetch_slabs now includes writer-segment frames whose bytes are fully below the flusher's disk boundary; prefetch_batch_body/prefetch_slab_body re-verify the frame end against the boundary under the header read (a pread over a partially-written tail would cache zeros for the unwritten part - the boundary check is what makes the warm cache trustworthy). Gates: 88/88 tests, enc_fp fp=6d240d7166cdda99 members=12130 bytes=9971843 byte-exact, jj verify 946/946 bad=0. v0.9.79 THE PREFETCH READS THE BUFFER: writer-segment frames past the flush boundary no longer wait for the disk - prefetch_batch_body/prefetch_slab_body read them THROUGH the append state (seg_read_body: the active buffer, the handoff queue, or landed disk bytes - whichever holds the record), so the warm cache covers 100% of the written frames instead of only the flushed suffix; a hole still fails the read cleanly, so zeros can never reach the warm cache. 0.9.78 CI verdict: 12/12 green, paper live rp99 766-1024 -> 475 us (x2), store write max 18.4 -> 4.1 ms (x4.4), warm region read 1399.6 -> 1967.7 MB/s, import 139.1 -> 210.1 MB/s (part runner speedup). Gates: 88/88 tests, enc_fp fp=6d240d7166cdda99 members=12130 bytes=9971843 byte-exact, jj verify 946/946 bad=0. v0.9.80 ZLIB-NG SERVE: the serve-stage timers named the wall - deflate 66% of every rendered region (read 33%, framing 0.3%), and the zlib-6 LEVEL is pinned by the sector format while the BACKEND never was. flate2 switches to the zlib-ng backend: same API, same stream format, 2.1x faster deflate at the same level - serve-micro A/B on the same host: 5.89 -> 9.66 MB/s (x1.64), deflate 283 -> 135 ms per 406-chunk region batch. The rendered bytes are only ever compared against the module's own views (identity pass, hook sampling) and re-imported by the module's own reader; a game client only inflates the entry. Gates: 88/88 tests, enc_fp fp=6d240d7166cdda99 members=12130 bytes=9971843 byte-exact, jj verify 946/946 bad=0. v0.9.81 INLINE TAIL CACHE: inline tails inflated zstd on every read - the 0.9.77 tail cache only covered Blob tails; decoding is a pure function of (dict, comp) so the same hash-keyed cache now serves inline tails too (xxh3 of the comp slice, dict id mixed into the key - warm repeats clone from RAM instead of inflating). SPEED stages-cold snapshot + reset added: the warm stage attribution used to accumulate the verify pass and the whole cold read (every first-touch inflate) into the warm floor. v0.9.82 WARM RESULT CACHE: a decoded chunk payload is cached keyed by the chunk key and stamped with the recipe record's (seg, off, len) - records commit once at a fixed location, segments are append-only with monotonic ids, so the stamp is the invalidation: any rewrite lands at a new record location and the stale entry can never match. Re-read chunks collapse from the whole decode pipeline (tail + slab slices + glob conversion + shift resolve + join, ~20 us) into one lookup + one memcpy. Pending (batched) recipes skip the cache - read-your-writes stays on the Arc body path.  Local A/B: warm p50 14.1 -> 1.6 us (x9), p99 62.5 -> 17.6 us (x3.6), warm stage meters all-zero (recipe/tail/slab/glob/join skipped). Two bugs found and fixed on the way: (1) a MutexGuard temporary of an `if let` scrutinee lives to the end of the statement (edition 2021) - re-locking in the miss branch self-deadlocked the reader; (2) the fused join path returned early, bypassing the cache store - region (fused-path) chunks never cached while whole-mode stores did (654 = exactly the entity warm reads). 16 MiB default thrashed on the 24.6 MB bench corpus (resc_hit=0, put+clone made warm SLOWER) - 64 MiB holds a full view-distance hot set; CSAVES_RESULT_CACHE bounds it, 0 disables. v0.9.83 VERIFY WALKER: the semantic comparator materialized the full per-voxel NAME vectors - 2 x 4096 cloned Strings per section pair (24 sections x 2 sides = ~196k string allocations per chunk) and deep-cloned the whole expected tree just to strip it; instrumented on the worst-case probe the walk was 82% of verify (5.5 of 6.8 ms per chunk). Now: expected tree stripped IN PLACE (owned Value, no clone) and palettes compared as u32 INDEX streams with a b->a palette remap built once per section (palette size, not voxel count; unused entries and out-of-range voxels keep the exact per-voxel string semantics via a sentinel + cold path). Local worst-case probe: verify A 28.3 -> 6.9 s, verify B 28.5 -> 7.0 s (x4.1, same ok/bad); the CI worst-case pole (two ~50 min verify passes) shrinks proportionally. Semantics byte-identical: 88/88 tests, jj verify 946/946 bad=0, bench verify 728+218 bad=0, enc_fp fp=6d240d7166cdda99 EXACT. v0.9.84 VERIFY WORLDGEN: the worst-case verify regenerated the expected chunk at 1.65 ms - the profile showed the per-voxel palette slot probe (a HashMap<&str,u8> SipHash-hashing the same 14 block names ~98k times per chunk) plus 2-3 splitmix cell hashes per voxel (~245k per chunk). Now: slot lookup is a fixed 14-wide array in first-seen order (identical palette and slot assignment), and the ore cells come from a once-per-process 4x4x96x3 table - the cells are chunk-independent (call sites pass cx=cz=0) and pure functions of (lx/4, lz/4, (y as u64)/4, tag), negative buckets included. wgen 1.65 -> 0.45 ms/chunk (x3.7), results identical (matched 512/512). Cumulative on the worst-case probe (4096 chunks): verify A 27.9 -> 3.4 s, verify B 28.3 -> 3.4 s (x8.2 vs 0.9.80, same ok=4096 bad=0) - the CI worst-case pole (two ~50 min verify passes) lands at ~1/8 of that. Test-side only: enc_fp fp=6d240d7166cdda99 EXACT, jj verify 946/946 bad=0, 88/88 tests. v0.9.85 MT LZMA2 COLD TIER: the pack sweep's cold-tier recompression ran liblzma's RAW single-threaded encoder - ~1-2 MB/s per stream - so one 10 MiB slab stream pinned a whole pack step's wall to itself (measured: 17.2 s of compression in 2 pack steps of a 16 MiB container; the rank-select MT policy never fired because it was tuned for zstd on 2-core runners). liblzma has no raw-LZMA2 MT encoder, so big streams now go through the blocked .xz MT encoder (same preset-6|EXTREME lzma2 filter chain, block size scaled to one block per worker) under a NEW codec stamp 0xFD; small streams keep the raw encoder + 0xFE. The stamp decision lives INSIDE the encoder helper and returns (stamp, bytes) - a raw stream under the MT stamp would land in the .xz decoder and corrupt (caught by the new roundtrip test before it could ship). Decode dispatch by stamp: old stores decode exactly as stored, .xz streams through the auto-detecting decoder. The 4-core MT gate is lifted for LZMA2 (2+ cores): the pole math differs 20x from zstd. Test-side only + pack-path: enc_fp fp=6d240d7166cdda99 EXACT, 89/89 tests (new MT roundtrip), jj verify 946/946 bad=0, worst-case verify bad=0 + ratio gates PASS. v0.9.86 CI HARDENING: the paper-bench console commands raced the server boot - a fixed `sleep 35` fired before a slow runner's Paper was accepting commands, so a run could execute NO forceload at all; the fetch sample starved (jvm fn=0, served=0 - the 0.9.82 paper-bench failure postmortem: the container held all 529 scanned chunks, the run simply never asked for them) and the meters gate failed on an empty sample. Every command-carrying run now gates on the server's own `Done (` line (readiness wait, capped 120 s) before feeding the console; dwell and stop timings unchanged. The failed job was rerun green against the same commit, confirming the flake class. v0.9.87 VERIFY STAGE TIMERS: the worst-case verify phases print gen/read/walk seconds at completion - the CI delta (verify B 1639 s vs verify A 1036 s on identical code, 60% slower) was not reproducible at local scale (4096 chunks: 1.1/0.2/2.0 s IDENTICAL for both phases), so the next run's timers answer it at 262144 scale. Zero product code touched. v0.9.88 READ-STAGE METERS AT SCALE: the 0.9.87 timers located the whole worst-case verify cost in read_chunk (A: 735 of 770 s; walk 31 s, gen 32 s - the walker fix holds) and showed phase B reads running 1.56x slower than A (5.83 vs 3.74 ms/chunk) - a delta the local probe cannot reproduce. Each verify phase now dumps the process-global read-stage meters (recipe/tail/resc/sectload/join/ glob/shift ns+counts) at 262144-chunk scale; the next run answers where B's extra 2 ms/chunk goes. v0.9.89 CRASH DURABILITY: accepted writes lived in RAM (writer buffer + pending recipe batch) until the 20 s maintenance sync or a save barrier - and a JVM exit NEVER runs the Rust Drop, so a killed server lost up to 20 s of player edits (the paper-bench 0.9.82 postmortem erased a whole run's container this way). The maintenance thread now runs a per-tick durability pass (2.5 s): commit the pending recipe batch (blocking drain - the batch record appends INTO the writer buffer, so the order is batch first, buffer second) then hand the buffer to the flusher thread. The data reaches the OS page cache in ~1 ms per tick: a process crash loses at most one tick; power-loss durability stays with sync_all's 20 s fsync cadence. Contract test: write, durability_tick, leak the store (the kill -9 shape), reopen - every chunk readable. 90/90 tests, enc_fp EXACT, jj verify 946/946 bad=0, liveab 1200/1200, batchstress ALL OK. v0.9.90 SIZE: tuned LZMA2 literal filter for cold slab streams - explicit lc=4 lp=0 pb=0 (preset 6|EXTREME defaults are lc=3 pb=2) under the new raw stamp 0xFC, measured -1.20% on the JJ member stream (904 466 B vs 915 488 B, 12 130 members, single 6.29 MiB slab group) at identical encode wall; lc/lp/pb are LZMA wire-format parts, so the tuned config gets its own stamp + decoder branch (preset-6 dict window unchanged on both) and legacy 0xFE streams keep decoding with the preset-6 defaults forever; the self-describing MT .xz path (0xFD) adopts the same tuned filter with no stamp change; delta pre-filter PROBED and rejected (+28..80% on the member stream - delta destroys the RLE/stride structure LZMA2 already models); CSAVES_LZMA_TUNE=0 mints legacy 0xFE again.
